text:
LOS ANGELES -- The Los Angeles Rams could be without both of their star wide receivers this week. All-Pro receiver Puka Nacua did not practice Friday and is questionable for Sunday's game against the Las Vegas Raiders after leaving practice early Thursday with a calf injury.

The Rams placed Davante Adams on injured reserve with a ruptured hamstring earlier this week. Adams is expected to miss six to 10 weeks.

Rams head coach Sean McVay called Nacua's injury "minor" but said he didn't know when or how it happened.

"He felt it where he wasn't able to have some of the power and explosion," McVay said. "He just kind of noticed it, but I don't think he was aware of any sort of specific play that led to it. He took part in a majority of the practice, left and got it checked out."

Adams' injury was expected to shift much of the volume of Los Angeles' passing game to Nacua, who had 129 receptions for 1,715 yards and 10 touchdowns in 2025 despite sharing the field with Adams for most of the season. Now, the Rams could be without the NFL's reigning leader in receptions (Nacua) and touchdown catches (Adams) from last season.

Nacua missed two games for a hip issue earlier this season before returning for the past three. He bounced back quickly, catching 32 passes for 343 yards and a touchdown in those three contests.

Nacua is in a contract year, as the Rams have held off on paying one of the league's top receivers as he proves he can grow from several off-the-field incidents. A second injury in seven weeks could bring the 25-year-old's future with the team into question, though an absence could also illustrate how much the Rams need him on offense.

If Nacua does not play, the Rams would need to rework a passing game built to lean heavily on Nacua and Adams. They would work with a group that includes Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington, Tutu Atwell and CJ Daniels. The most productive among them this season has been Mumpfield, who has eight catches for 127 yards and a touchdown. Whittington, Atwell and Daniels have combined for just five catches for 43 yards.

Los Angeles opted not to spend significant resources on another wide receiver this offseason despite needing one after last year's narrow loss to the Seattle Seahawks in the NFC Championship Game. The Rams traded up to draft Daniels in the sixth round out of Miami, but he has been a healthy scratch for all six games. They traded running back Jarquez Hunter to bring back Atwell, a previous starter in Los Angeles, but he has been active for just three games and has caught three passes for 31 yards.

The injuries could lead to more targets for running backs Kyren Williams and Blake Corum, both of whom have flashed as receivers. It could also put a heavier load on the tight ends, though the Rams are missing their top receiving option there in Terrance Ferguson, who is on IR with an ankle injury.

The lack of receiving options for Matthew Stafford should mean a heavier dose of a run game that has been efficient but hasn't seen much volume yet for Williams and Corum.

The injury news has been a wave crashing over the Rams since their 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals, which dropped them to 2-4. In addition to Adams, they also placed defensive end Kobie Turner and defensive tackle Poona Ford on IR, with Ford's season being over.

Cornerback Trent McDuffie is also questionable to face the Raiders with a groin injury after not practicing this week and missing last week's game against the Cardinals.

text:
We've been holding our breath ever since Chicago Bears tight end Cole Kmet exited the Week 7 game against the New England Patriots early with a knee injury.

It did not look good right off the bat, as Kmet had to be carted off the field in the fourth quarter after going down. Then, after the game, head coach Ben Johnson admitted it didn't look good.

Now, on Friday, we have the update we were fearing.

Johnson addressed the media on Friday afternoon and confirmed that Kmet has a serious knee injury and it is indeed a season-ending issue.

"He’s everything we want to be about here. He’s going to be sorely missed. He’s Chicago. He’s been here his whole life. He’s a big part of our heartbeat. It stinks. It does. I hate it for him," Johnson said.

Now, one has to wonder if Thursday night might have been the last time we see Kmet in a Bears uniform.

He does have one more year left on his contract in 2027, but he also has a hefty $15.4 million cap number and the Bears have a clear out in his contract. He'll almost certainly need to redo the deal to stay.

What Kmet's injury means for Bears

Losing Kmet is a huge blow for the Bears, and in more ways than one.

Even as the No. 2 tight end behind Colston Loveland, Kmet still sees a big role on offense, as evidenced by his 62% snap share. That's because the Bears run 12 and 13 personnel at the third- and fourth-highest rates in the NFL, per Sumer Sports.

We already know he's a plus pass-catcher, but Kmet is also one of the team's best blockers among skill-position players and the importance of his blocking extends to special teams, and specifically on the field goal unit.

Kmet's injury will push rookie tight end and third-round pick Sam Roush into a bigger role, which is concerning because Roush has seen plenty of struggles during his first season in the NFL.

As a pass-catcher, Roush has dropped two passes, which is 40% of his targets, and he has had issues with blocking at times. To make matters worse, Roush has committed three penalties, according to NFLPenalties.com.

Another tight end is needed

The Bears don't have a fourth tight end on their active roster, so they'll need to add another. Chicago has two options on the practice squad in Stephen Carlson and Qadir Ismail.

The most likely approach will be the Bears promoting Carlson over Ismail given the former's advantage in experience, which will be needed in Chicago's young tight ends room.

Carlson has 28 games of experience under his belt while Ismail has never taken a regular-season snap in the NFL. Carlson isn't going to offer anything as a pass-catcher, but he is a sufficient blocker.

Given the Bears' heavy reliance on tight ends, it would not shock us to see the team bring in more help via free-agent signing or a minor trade, but chances are they'll likely asses things over the next few weeks ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline before potentially making a move.

title: Anton Harrison's Injury Could Have Major Repercussions for These 4 Jaguars
description:
The Jacksonville Jaguars were dealt a tough blow on Friday, with reports stating the Jaguars' left tackle is set to miss the rest of the 2026 season due to an ACL injury.
The domino effect from Harrison's injury could be significant for a number of members on the roster as a result.
Which Jaguars are set to be most impacted by Harrison's injuty, and why?

text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Anton Harrison is done for the rest of the season.

The Jacksonville Jaguars were dealt a tough blow on Friday, with reports stating the Jaguars' left tackle is set to miss the rest of the 2026 season due to an ACL injury.

The domino effect from Harrison's injury could be significant for a number of members on the roster as a result. Which Jaguars are set to be most impacted by Harrison's injuty, and why? We break it down below.

Anton Harrison

This one is clear. Harrison was entering an absolutely pivotal 2026 season, not just because he was made the team's blindside protector for the first time but because of the timing of his switch to left tackle. Harrison, who had his fifth-year option picked up for next season, was set to be a potential benefactor from the move to left tackle considering what a strong season could have meant for him when it came to his contract and what the talks at the table look like.

Harrison will of course return in 2027, but he will be coming off an ACL injury and will have just a six-game sample size as an NFL left tackle entering the season. This doesn't mean Harrison can't still play himself into a big-time deal with the Jaguars moving forward, but the situation has seen a major wrench thrown into it. The Jaguars needed this season to see if Harrison was worth extending, and Harrison needed this season to prove he should be one of the NFL's highest-paid tackles. Now, neither side is going to get much clarity entering the 2027 season.

Daniele Faalele

It feels unlikely that the Jaguars will play Daniel Faalele much at the tackle position since he is a more natural guard and has subsequently taken more snaps at the guard position over the course of his career. But Faalele, who the Jaguars traded for during training camp as they sustained a rash of offensive line injuries, has been a healthy scratch for the Jaguars in each game this season as they entered each contest with eight active offensive linemen. With Harrison out, Faalele now becomes OL8.

Does this mean Faalele is set to enter the Jaguars' starting lineup soon post-bye? No, not really. But he will at the very least be active and be closer to stepping onto the field than he was before. Faalele is unlikely to be needed unless the Jaguars sustain more injuries along the offensive line, but he should now at the least be an option for the Jaguars to turn to on game day, especially in jumbo packages since Wyatt Milum's role as the No. 6 lineman may now change.

Patrick Mekari

This could be an interesting development for Jaguars offensive lineman Patrick Mekari, who Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said was getting closer to returning from injured reserve after missing all of training camp and the first six games of the season with a back injury. Mekari has dealt with injuries for most of his time with the Jaguars, but he could give them some very real offensive line depth when he is off injured reserve, especially in the context of the Jaguars' swing tackle spot.

Mekari has nearly 2,000 career snaps at the tackle positions since joining the NFL in 2019, giving him a significantly larger sample size at the tackle position than any of the Jaguars' other in-house options for swing tackle. Mekari has been a disappointment with the Jaguars since becoming their highest-paid free agent of the new regime in March 2025, but the loss of Harrison could give him the chance to prove his worth.

Mekari of course has to get healthy first, but once he is healthy he should give the Jaguars a boost in terms of a versatile and experienced depth option. Considering the Jaguars' top swing tackle, Walker Little, is now the team's starting left tackle, then Mekari has suddenly become much more valuable to the Jaguars than he was at the start of the season.

Wyatt Milum

The Jaguars have not had a ton of need for Wyatt Milum to step into the lineup since they drafted him in the third-round of the 2025 NFL Drafft, but he now looks like he is one snap away from likely becoming the Jaguars' starting right tackle. Milum was set to be the Jaguars' top swing tackle at the start of the season if Cole Van Lanen was set to miss time at the start of the year, which of course did not end up happening. But the Jaguars are now right back into the same situation with Harrison out for the year.

Milum has played just 122 snaps on offense in his career thus far, with many of those snaps coming as an extra offensive lineman in jumbo packages. That is a good bit different than potentially lining up at offensive tackle against some of the best pass-rushers in the NFL, but that is the scenario the Jaguars have now found themselves in. Milum went from a luxury player to a critical part of the depth chart now that Harrison is sidelined for the rest of 2026.

4:07pm: Edmunds has a torn muscle in his chest, a source told ESPN’s Jordan Raanan, who backs Duggan in reporting he is done for the year.

3:08pm: In yet another major blow to the Giants, linebacker Tremaine Edmunds will miss the rest of the season with a shoulder injury, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports. He joins quarterback Jaxson Dart and pass rusher Brian Burns as key Giants who will not return from injuries this season.

Edmunds was a big-ticket offseason signing for the Giants, who brought in the former Bill and Bear on a three-year, $36MM contract to replace the released Bobby Okereke. While playing all 380 of the Giants’ defensive snaps over their first six games, Edmunds piled up 50 tackles (three for loss) and added three quarterback hits, two sacks and a pair of pass breakups. The ninth-year veteran and two-time Pro Bowler has never finished with fewer than 100 tackles in a season, but that streak will come to an end in 2026.

Fortunately for the Giants, their offseason moves to address the off-ball linebacker position went beyond adding Edmunds. They also drafted Arvell Reese fifth overall and re-signed Micah McFadden to a one-year, $3.75MM deal. Reese has held his own alongside Edmunds as a full-time starter, but he will now pair with McFadden. While McFadden suffered a season-ending foot injury in Week 1 in 2025, he was a regular starter in the Giants’ defense over his first four years.

McFadden has played just two snaps on defense in 2026, but he will now have an opportunity to reclaim a significant role in Edmunds’ place. Jack Kelly, Malik Harrison and Zaire Barnes, who are primarily special-teamers, and practice squad member Chandler Martin are the team’s other options at the position. With the Nov. 10 trade deadline coming up, Big Blue could look for help to fill Edmunds’ void. At 3-2-1, the Giants are in first place in an underwhelming NFC East and could end up as buyers. They have just over $8MM in cap space, which ranks 19th in the NFL.

Speaking of cap space, the Giants guaranteed Edmunds $23.7MM, including $11.35MM in base salary in 2027. His cap number will climb from $5.56MM to a far less palatable $16.17MM, though releasing him before June 1 would cost the Giants $2.52MM in space and leave them with $18.69MM in dead money. Designating Edmunds a post-June 1 release would leave New York with $15.02MM in dead cap, but the team would pick up $1.15MM in spending room. That’s not to say the Giants will move on from Edmunds, but they could consider it in the wake of an injury-ruined season.

Doesn't make alot of sense to activate him, while having to cut someone else like Cody White who plays ST, if Thornton isn't going to be playing significant snaps on Sundays.

Per google ..

An NFL team cannot place a player on season-ending Injured Reserve (IR) if they are healthy, even after completing a 21-day practice window.

The same foundational rules apply at every stage of the IR process: a player must have a legitimate, documented medical condition to be placed on any version of the Injured Reserve list.

What Happens if the 21-Day Window Expires?

When a player is designated to return from IR and begins practicing, a 21-day clock starts. By the end of those 21 days, the team must make a decision based on the player's health and roster status:

If the player is healthy: The team must activate them to the 53-man roster. If they do not want to use a roster spot on the healthy player, they must release or waive them.

If the team takes no action: If the 21 days expire and the team fails to activate the player, the player automatically reverts to IR for the remainder of the season. Doing this intentionally for a healthy player to "stash" them is a violation of league rules and constitutes roster manipulation.

So, it appears Thornton will be activated to the 53 next week or he'll be waived.

If he's waived I would be shocked if he's not claimed immediately, plenty of teams out there will find space for a WR of his size/speed, young with 2+ years left on a rookie contract.

OTOH if this was Kubiak's plan they probably let him go before the season.

Since they can't IR him (because he's healthy) and Kubiak made a point to say he is, I am now leaning more towards they will activate him and release Cody White, who is a vested vet and isn't subject to waivers. They can then re-sign him immediately to the PS, if he chooses to, and he is then eligible for another 3 game-callups.

Will be interesting to see what they do.

HENDERSON, Nev.-- The Las Vegas Raiders (3-3) are playing host to the Los Angeles Rams (2-4) on Sunday at Allegiant Stadium.

To say the Raider Nation is excited about this football game would be an enormous understatement.

But ahead of the big renewal of the rivalry, the Raiders got some concerning news in their latest injury report.

The Rookie Rusher

Rookie RB Mike Washington Jr. is a key part of the heralded 2026 Silver and Black rookie class, and the fan base has been clamoring for more of him with each successful performance.

Earlier this week, I asked Kubiak, who constantly preaches to his team about earning more reps, if Washington Jr. had earned more; he said yes. The Raider Nation was elated, as they stand united about needing to get the run game going.

Kubiak explained what the Arkansas Razorback had done to earn those reps.

“He's putting the work in, and you see the practice come to life in the game. ”

Late Thursday, Mike Washington Jr. showed up on the injury report and was listed as not participating.

On Wednesday, he was listed with a foot/back injury and was limited, but he did not participate on Thursday. That change is very significant.

What This Means

Klint Kubiak likes to give players opportunities in games after successful practices. While it is not impossible, Kubiak’s track record makes it seem improbable that if Washington Jr. doesn’t practice on Friday, he would play on Sunday. That is purely speculative and not from the team; it is simply an inference from Kubiak’s previous statements and implications.

Search for Significance

Since day one, Washington Jr. has been Ashton Jeanty's backup. But he continues to expand his team's trust in him with each successful play.

We will learn more late Friday morning when I speak to Kubiak and ask him for an update. The 'Raiders' run game has struggled this season, and Mike Washington Jr. was a big reason for optimism that it would take off.

text:
CHICAGO (AP) — The Chicago Bears like their group of tight ends, and the position plays a major role in coach Ben Johnson's offense.

That depth is about to be tested.

Chicago will be without Cole Kmet for the rest of the season after he hurt his right knee on a reception with 5:34 left in Thursday night's 30-24 win over New England. It's the first major injury for Kmet since the Illinois native was selected by the Bears in the second round of the 2020 draft out of Notre Dame.

“He’s going to be sorely missed. Really, he’s Chicago,” Johnson said Friday. “He’s been here his whole life and he’s a big part of our heartbeat. So, it stinks, it does, I hate it for him, I hate it for his teammates as well. And yet the train keeps rolling along. Someone else has to step up.”

Kmet had just 10 catches for 87 yards and a touchdown in seven games this season, but his value to the Bears (5-2) goes beyond his personal numbers. He has been a dependable blocker for Chicago's potent rushing attack, and his versatility has created more flexibility with how the team deploys the rest of its tight ends.

Kmet's injury comes with Colston Loveland beginning to heat up after a slow start to the season. The second-year tight end has 13 receptions for 134 yards and two touchdowns in his last two games.

“He’s come on," Johnson said. “The target share’s gone up a little bit. He’s done a really nice job. He’s getting open.”

Kmet's absence likely means a bigger role for rookie Sam Roush, a third-round pick in the draft out of Stanford. The Bears also have Stephen Carlson and Qadir Ismail on their practice squad, and Hayden Large could be activated at some point after beginning the season on injured reserve.

Roush, 23, has three receptions for 33 yards in seven games.

“We’ve been very pleased with the improvement that he’s made over these first seven weeks,” Johnson said. “There’s a high likelihood that his rep count is going to go up as a result of what’s going on here. ... Very smart player. He had some rookie hiccups early in the season, like everybody does, and yet he learns. He doesn’t make the same mistake twice.”

What's working

Caleb Williams posted another impressive performance in his second game back since being sidelined by a right hamstring injury. He was 22 for 33 for 308 yards and two touchdowns.

Williams became the third quarterback in franchise history to throw for 300-plus yards in back-to-back wins, joining Sid Luckman in 1947 and Billy Wade in 1962.

What needs help

There has been some inconsistency with Chicago's secondary. The Bears allowed Jordan Love to pass for 367 yards and two touchdowns in a 31-7 loss at Green Bay on Oct. 11, and they also struggled with Drake Maye in the win over New England. Maye threw for 321 yards and two TDs.

Stock up

Rome Odunze had three receptions for 63 yards — in the fourth quarter. He had six catches for 79 yards over the previous two games combined.

The 24-year-old Odunze played a major role in Chicago's drive to Cairo Santos' 58-yard field goal with 1:34 left. With the Bears facing third-and-9 from their own 10, Odunze made a terrific catch on a 21-yard gain. After D’Andre Swift lost 2 yards on a first-down carry, Odunze had another 21-yard reception.

Stock down

Jaylon Johnson had a rough night. The cornerback whiffed when he tried to tackle Maye on a 15-yard scramble with 3:32 left in the second quarter. He had a similar issue on Rhamondre Stevenson's 48-yard touchdown reception on the final play of the first half. He also was called for pass interference on New England's last drive of the game.

Injuries

Besides Kmet's departure against the Patriots, Chicago also lost cornerback Malik Muhammad to a toe injury. There was no update on his status on Friday.

Key number

71% — Williams' 71% completion rate ranks second in the NFL among qualified passers, going into this weekend's action. He completed 58.1% of his passes last season.

Up next

The Bears don’t play again until they visit Seattle on Nov. 2. The last time the teams played, Jason Myers kicked two first-half field goals to send the Seahawks to an ugly 6-3 win at Soldier Field on Dec. 26, 2024. Following the trip to Seattle, the Bears host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Nov. 8.

Lamar Jackson's Status Yet To Be Determined

The Ravens have yet to rule Lamar Jackson out of Sunday's clash with the Cincinnati Bengals.

Jackson, who revealed on Friday that he's been dealing with a high ankle sprain, said he's "heading in the right direction" for Sunday, per ESPN's Jamison Hensley.

Ravens head coach Jesse Minter wouldn't commit either way on Jackson's status when he addressed the media on Friday.

The Ravens posted a 1-1 record without Jackson so far this season. Tyler Huntley led them to an overtime win over the Atlanta Falcons. They then lost to the Cleveland Browns in Week 6.

If Jackson plays, the assumption would be that he doesn't run as much to put more pressure on the ankle. He may be more inclined to sit back in the pocket and throw, or rely more on Derrick Henry to carry the offensive load.

The Bengals allowed over 300 total yards in four of their first five games. They let up over 100 rushing yards in their three games prior to their Week 6 bye.

It's an ideal matchup for Henry, regardless of who the quarterback is, but if Jackson plays, the forecast for the Baltimore pass-catchers is better.

Jackson passed for over 200 yards in three of his four starts. He completed 75 percent of his passes in his last two games before the injury.

Huntley threw for 366 yards in the last two weeks. He was better against Atlanta and struggled a bit against Cleveland in a tougher matchup.

Huntley is a solid replacement for Jackson in fantasy football, if he starts for a third straight week. The matchup against Cincinnati should allow Huntley to put up a similar stat line to the Atlanta game.

Puka Nacua is officially listed as questionable for the Rams' Week 7 battle with the Las Vegas Raiders.

Nacua left practice on Thursday with a calf issue. That ailment kept him out of practice on Friday.

Nacua's potential absence would be a massive blow to the Rams offense, a unit that is already without Davante Adams for an extended period of time.

Matthew Stafford's fantasy value would crater if Nacua and Adams, arguably the best wide receiver tandem in the NFL, aren't on the field.

Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell and Jordan Whittington are next up on the wide receiver depth chart for the Rams.

However, it might be smarter to go with Blake Corum, Tyler Higbee or Colby Parkinson

description:
CHICAGO -- Bears tight end Cole Kmet will miss the remainder of the 2026 season after he suffered a serious right knee injury during Chicago's 30-24 win over New England, coach Ben Johnson announced Friday.
The Bears placed Kmet on season-ending injured reserve following testing Friday morning after he was unable to bear weight on his leg.
The tight end immediately grabbed for his knee and had to be carted to the locker room.

text:
CHICAGO -- Bears tight end Cole Kmet will miss the remainder of the 2026 season after he suffered a serious right knee injury during Chicago's 30-24 win over New England, coach Ben Johnson announced Friday.

The Bears placed Kmet on season-ending injured reserve following testing Friday morning after he was unable to bear weight on his leg. In seven games, Kmet had 10 catches for 87 yards and a touchdown.

"He's everything we want to be about here," Johnson said. "He's one of the glue guys. He's one of the guys that I can count on, whether it's a messaging standpoint or getting the pulse of the team. He's going to be sorely missed."

With 5:46 to play in the fourth quarter, Kmet caught an 8-yard pass from Caleb Williams before colliding with Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez and linebacker Robert Spillane as he ran up the Bears' sideline. The tight end immediately grabbed for his knee and had to be carted to the locker room.

Current and former teammates, including Patriots safety Kevin Byard III, gathered around Kmet as he was loaded onto a cart. He gave the crowd a thumbs-up as he was transported through the northwest tunnel inside Soldier Field.

"It stinks, it does. I hate it for him. I hate it for his teammates as well," Johnson said. "And yet the train keeps rolling along. Someone else has to step up."

Kmet, 27, was drafted by the Bears in 2020 and has missed only one game over his seven NFL seasons. He has logged the eighth-highest snap count on offense (62.19%) this season and joined Hall of Famer Mike Ditka on Thursday as just the second tight end in franchise history to top 3,000 career receiving yards after he caught three passes for 28 yards.

He saw a role shift since Johnson took over in 2025 but remained a vital piece of the Bears' operation despite his production as a pass catcher dipping.

Without Kmet, Chicago will lean into Colston Loveland and rookie Sam Roush. Other options further down the Bears' depth chart are Stephen Carlson and Qadir Ismail on the practice squad and undrafted free agent Hayden Large, who is eligible to come off injured reserve.

The Bears play some of the highest rates of 12 and 13 personnel (multiple-TE sets) in the NFL. While Kmet's absence will undoubtedly be felt in a multitude of ways, Johnson said the offense won't change, particularly what it asks of its tight ends.

"We trained all our tight ends to be able to do all the jobs," Johnson said. "I don't see us really changing who we are or what we do as a result of that. ... There's a lot of solutions out there to make sure that we can still run the ball, pass protect and our route running, I think we're gonna be OK."

text:
Jacksonville Jaguars left tackle Anton Harrison will miss the remainder of the season after tearing a ligament in his right knee.

Harrison injured his knee during a win against the Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London on Oct. 11. He spun on the field turf to make a block and twisted his knee when he planted his right leg. Harrison was carted to the locker room.

Harrison waited until the Jaguars (4-2) returned from two weeks overseas to have arthroscopic surgery to determine the extent of the damage. The scope Wednesday revealed a torn anterior cruciate ligament.

Jacksonville already placed Harrison on injured reserve.

Backup Walker Little, who has started 40 games over six seasons with Jacksonville, is expected to replace Harrison in the lineup the rest of the season.

Harrison has started 53 games for the Jaguars since they selected him 27th overall in the 2023 NFL Draft. The former Oklahoma Sooners standout moved from right tackle to left tackle this season in hopes of improving Jacksonville’s run game, which ranks 14th this season, up from 20th in 2025.

Harrison is Jacksonville's first starter to sustain a season-ending injury in 2026.

title: Colts' Tyler Warren to miss second game with groin injury - ESPN
authors: Stephen Holder, Nick Suss, Jenna Laine, Rich Cimini, Courtney Cronin, Nate Taylor, Brady Henderson, Josh Weinfuss, Tim McManus, Turron Davenport
description:
INDIANAPOLIS -- Tight end Tyler Warren will miss his second consecutive game with a groin injury when the Indianapolis Colts travel to face the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday.
Warren sustained the injury in practice last week and was ruled out hours before the Week 6 loss to Tennessee.

The Dallas Cowboys are dealing with an injury at wide receiver that opens the door for one of the team's preseason superstars to make his NFL debut in Week 7.

That injury is to wide receiver and returner KaVontae Turpin, who is dealing with a ribs injury he suffered in Week 6. Turpin did not take part in practice on Thursday.

Furthermore, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reports that Turpin is dealing with "cartilage damage" and will "probably" miss at least this week, when the Cowboys face the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night.

"Cowboys receiver/returner KaVontae Turpin suffered an injury to his ribs Sunday, and one source believes he's dealing with cartilage damage," Fowler wrote.

"He will probably miss this week and go from there," he added.

Time for Camden Brown's debut?

The Cowboys have carried five receivers into gamedays for every contest this season. Turpin being ruled out would lessen that number to four, unless they dress Camden Brown, who has remained inactive for every game this season.

Dallas' offense has sputtered of late. Perhaps the Cowboys should not only dress Brown, who was electric during the preseason, but also give him some snaps.

Brown also has special teams experience after playing in that area during the preseason, so that gives him added value and a better chance to finally see the field in Week 7.

Camden Brown's electric offseason

An undrafted free-agent signing of the Cowboys after the 2026 NFL Draft, Brown was a menace against Dallas defense in camp (that doesn't hold as much weight as it once did with how badly the Cowboys' defense has played, but I digress) and he then carried that into the preseason with electric showings.

The 6-foot-2, 204-pound wide receiver tallied three catches for 62 yards and two touchdowns in preseason Week 1, and followed that up with two catches for 77 yards in the second exhibition contest.

“The game’s not too big for him. He does it every day in practice, we see it all the time," head coach Brian Schottenheimer stated. "Really good day, but he’s got to keep stacking what he’s been doing."

But it wasn't just about the totals for Brown, who made some "this guy belongs in the league" kinds of catches along the way.

Brown cooled off in the final preseason game with just one catch for 27 yards, but he had done enough to state his case and the Cowboys ended up keeping him against all odds because the expectation all offseason was the team would only carry five wideouts with how top-heavy it was.

Cowboys fans have been wanting to see Brown all season long after the impressive display he had during the offseason.

With Turpin likely to sit, it's time to free Camden Brown and let him play some snaps on offense, too.

title: Ravens will take wait-and-see approach with Lamar Jackson - The Baltimore Banner
description:

Before his injury, Jackson was the engine of one of the NFL’s best offenses.

text:
Join the huddle. Sign up here for Ravens updates in your inbox.

Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson said Friday he’s “heading in the right direction” in his recovery from a high-ankle sprain that has sidelined him the past two games, but he’s considered questionable for Sunday’s showdown against the Cincinnati Bengals.

Jackson, who returned to practice this week for the first time since spraining his left ankle in the Ravens’ Oct. 4 win over the Tennessee Titans, said after practice Friday that his availability could be a game-time decision. Although Jackson said he wouldn’t need to feel 100% healthy Sunday to play, he wouldn’t feel comfortable if his mobility were severely limited.

“I’m hurting,” Jackson said in his first comments since the injury. “I’m trying to help my team win, but I’m not to my full capability. I’m not even close to it. But I’m just trying.”

Jackson called his injury, which he suffered when Titans defensive end Jermaine Johnson landed on the outside of his ankle just before halftime in Week 4, “very, very, very, very, very painful.” The severity of Jackson’s high-ankle sprain is unclear, but even minor sprains in the NFL typically sideline players for at least a month.

Jackson said the swelling in his ankle has receded “a lot” and that his pain levels and mobility would determine his readiness for Sunday.

“I’m just trying to move how I move,” said Jackson, who was limited in practice throughout the week and noted he can’t put “too much pressure” on his ankle when he runs. “If I can’t do that, I can’t help my team. I can’t put my team in a situation like that. I feel like I’m doing a disservice then.”

The Ravens will be without starting outside linebacker Tavius Robinson, who suffered a season-ending pectoral injury in Sunday’s loss to the Cleveland Browns, coach Jesse Minter said Friday. Robinson, the team’s leader in sacks (3.5), has played 72.4% of the Ravens’ defensive snaps and is in the final year of his rookie deal. Rookie Zion Young, a second-round pick, is expected to step into Robinson’s role as an edge-setting run stopper.

Starting safety Jaylinn Hawkins will also miss Sunday’s game with a knee injury, which first surfaced in practice Wednesday. Minter said the injury is not believed to be long term. Keondre Jackson, a special teams stalwart who’s played just one defensive snap this season, could earn more playing time. The Ravens could also move safety Kyle Hamilton back to a deep-lying role next to Malaki Starks and start a cornerback in the slot.

If Lamar Jackson is unavailable Sunday, backup Tyler Huntley would make his third consecutive start at quarterback. He’s 1-1 this season, impressing late in the Ravens’ overtime win over the Atlanta Falcons and struggling throughout a narrow loss Sunday to the Browns. The Ravens finished with season lows in points (10) and total yards (235) in their AFC North opener.

Before his injury, Jackson was the engine of one of the NFL’s best offenses. The Ravens have averaged 6.9 yards per play with the two-time NFL Most Valuable Player on the field this season, a mark that would lead the league, and just 4.8 yards with him off the field (23rd), according to the NFL’s Next Gen Stats.

Jackson’s injury came under scrutiny last week after he missed practice while being what Minter called “day-to-day” in his recovery. He also missed the start of practice Wednesday before rejoining the team late in the session, working out in Ravens shorts and a Ravens hooded jacket.

“I think, if Lamar can play, it’d be great,” cornerback Marlon Humphrey said after practice Thursday. “If he doesn’t, we have ‘Snoop’ [Huntley], but it seems like Lamar’s the only quarterback that kind of gets the slander that he gets for anytime anything is going on. I feel like you just don’t see these same articles and you don’t see these same headlines. I think it’s unfair treatment.”

Said Jackson on Friday: “It’s going to always be that way. It’s been that way. No matter what Lamar’s doing, there’s going to be something said, so it is what it is.”

Jackson ramped up Thursday, when he was on the field for the start of practice and led the Ravens’ quarterbacks through position drills, his ankle wrapped in athletic tape. His workload in Friday’s media viewing period was limited to half-speed work with the offensive line and running backs. He wasn’t on the field with teammates as practice ended, and he required treatment afterward.

Minter said the Ravens would decide on Jackson’s availability by assessing his comfort with the injury, his confidence in playing and evaluations from the team’s medical staff. Jackson said Friday that playing through a series of injuries last year was “dumb, a little bit.”

His status could remain uncertain through late Sunday morning, when the Ravens must decide whether to activate him. Jackson said he hoped to feel better this weekend and reiterated that he was working to “get the little cobwebs out of it as much as possible.” He indicated that there was still pain in his ankle when he planted his left foot.

Healthy or not, Jackson would face a stiff test Sunday at M&T Bank Stadium. Cincinnati (3-2) enters Week 7 off a bye and has the NFL’s No. 13 defense, according to FTN. The Bengals’ much-improved pass rush would test not only Jackson’s mobility but also the Ravens’ remade offensive line.

Jackson would likely start behind Cam Jurgens, his fourth different center of the season, who was acquired in an Oct. 7 trade but wasn’t cleared to practice until Wednesday because he was in the NFL’s concussion protocol.

“That guy’s smart,” Jackson said. “He’s calling out stuff already. I was shocked. I’m like, ‘Damn, he’s a pro.’ I’m looking forward to playing with Cam. It’s going to be great.”

The Ravens, who had one of the NFL’s easiest schedules over the season’s first six weeks, can’t afford to lose ground in the AFC or the division over the next month-plus. After Cincinnati, the Ravens will face the Buffalo Bills, Jacksonville Jaguars, Los Angeles Chargers, Carolina Panthers and Houston Texans before their Week 13 bye.

For now, though, the Ravens are taking a wait-and-see approach. Huntley shrugged Friday when a reporter asked whether he expected the decision on Jackson’s status to come Sunday.

“I just have to be ready to play Sunday,” Huntley said, “if that’s the case.”

Note

Cornerback T.J. Tampa (knee), who was designated to return off injured reserve, is doubtful for Sunday’s game. He would first have to be activated off IR to make his season debut. Defensive lineman Broderick Washington, who missed the Ravens’ loss in Cleveland with an ankle injury, is questionable after being limited in practice this week.

text:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- The New York Jets' struggling offense will get one or possibly two key players back in the lineup Sunday.

Wide receiver Adonai Mitchell, sidelined four games with a right-hand finger injury that required a surgical procedure, practiced all week and will play against the Miami Dolphins (0-5), coach Aaron Glenn said Friday.

The Jets are hopeful that running back Breece Hall also will return after missing three games with a quadriceps injury, but there's less certainty in his case. Hall, who practiced the past two days on a limited basis, is questionable for the game. Glenn said they will make the decision Sunday.

They could use a spark. The Jets (2-4) are averaging only 18.7 points per game (27th), with only four touchdowns in the past three games.

With Mitchell back, the Jets will have their top three receivers for the first time since Week 1. Mitchell, Garrett Wilson and rookie Omar Cooper Jr. have been on the field together for only four snaps -- the first series of the season opener. Cooper missed the next four games with an ankle injury, returning last week with a six-catch, 103-yard performance.

"Anytime we get the band back together, when they're all there and they get a chance to continue to build this relationship on the field, it's always critical," Glenn said, alluding to Mitchell's return.

Mitchell made nine receptions for 123 yards in the first two games. Before Week 3, he sustained a significant finger injury in practice when he caught it in a teammate's jersey, Glenn said. He practiced the next day. The Jets didn't think he'd be sidelined that long, so they didn't put him on injured reserve. About 10 days later, Mitchell underwent a procedure.

"With all the playmakers that we have, when you have a guy like AD out there, he can stretch the field, he can be a possession guy, and I think him, Garrett, Coop, they just present a lot of different challenges for the defense," quarterback Geno Smith said. "And so the more guys, the merrier."

Braelon Allen has filled in nicely for Hall, rushing for 253 yards over the last three games. Hall remains the starter, according to Glenn, adding that Allen will continue to get carries.

Left guard Dylan Parham, out three games with a knee injury, also could return Sunday. He returned to practice this week and is listed as questionable. The Jets could have their entire starting lineup intact for the first time since Week 1.

Glenn declined to comment on a report, confirmed by ESPN, that he was fined $250,000 by the league for his conduct toward game officials.

"I will keep that between me, the NFL and the refs," Glenn said.

GREEN BAY, Wis. -- First Edgerrin Cooper, now Zaire Franklin. The Green Bay Packers have lost another inside linebacker due to injury, although at least the latest one is not season-ending.

Franklin won't play Sunday against the Detroit Lions because of a shin injury he sustained in practice Thursday.

"Unfortunately there was a little collision," Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Friday. "He got kneed in the shin, so he's going to be out this game."

LaFleur said Franklin is not expected to go on injured reserve, meaning he will miss fewer than four games. Although it's his first year with the Packers after coming to Green Bay in an offseason trade with the Colts, the ninth-year veteran quickly became a key part of the defense. He was elected defensive captain, rare for someone in the first year with a team, and has been the signal-caller for the defense.

Franklin ranks second on the team in tackles (41) and has two quarterback hits, a forced fumble and a pass breakup.

The Packers lost Cooper three weeks ago to a torn Achilles, so they will have to face Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs without both of their starting inside linebackers. Gibbs ranks second in the NFL in yards from scrimmage per game (149.4) and fourth in rushing yards per game (100.8).

The Packers used two players to replace Cooper: Isaiah McDuffie and Ty'Ron Hopper. McDuffie has started but Hopper has played almost as many snaps in the rotation the last two weeks. Now Hopper, who had an interception in Week 5 against the Bears, will get a chance to start, too.

"He's done a great job," LaFleur said of Hopper. "His progression has been pretty cool to watch, just how he's developed over the years, especially I think we kind of got a good sense early on in training camp that he's on his way, so this will be a great opportunity for him to get even more reps."

On the offensive side, running back Josh Jacobs is on track to make his season debut Sunday. He missed the first six games while on the commissioner exempt list and practiced this week for the first time since training camp.

"Yeah, I believe so," LaFleur said when asked if Jacobs is on track to play against the Lions. "But again, we'll get through it and see how he's feeling and the confidence he has in himself, which I think is pretty strong. But those conversations will take place after [Friday's] practice."

text:
Trevor Lawrence's blind side protector, Anton Harrison, is done for the rest of the season due to a torn ACL. Harrison underwent arthroscopic surgery on Thursday, but during the surgery, doctors discovered he had torn his ACL as well, according to ESPN.

Harrison, 24, hurt his knee in Week 5 during Jacksonville's eventual win over the Eagles in London and was carted off. The Jaguars, who also played in London in Week 6, placed Harrison on IR but were hopeful he'd be able to return at some point this season. Then Thursday's surgery revealed the full scope of the injury.

The No. 27 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, Harrison moved from right tackle to left tackle this offseason. It had been a bit of an up-and-down year for him in his new spot -- he allowed three sacks and 12 pressures in just five games -- but it's a significant loss for Jacksonville nonetheless.

Veteran swing Walker Little took over for Harrison in Week 5 and started in his stead in Week 6 against the Texans. The good news for Jacksonville is that Little has significant experience (40 career starts) and performed ably -- no sacks, two pressures allowed -- in Week 6 against a ferocious Houston front.

The bad news, outside the obvious bad news that comes with losing a left tackle, is this leaves Jacksonville paper-thin at tackle. Little was the only tackle on the roster outside Harrison and starting right tackle Cole Van Lanen. The Jaguars do have veteran offensive lineman Geron Christian Sr. on the practice squad but could look to make moves ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

Jaguars options

Roll with Walker Little

A second-round pick out of Stanford in 2021, Little has spent his entire career with the Jaguars, and he started at least three games every year from 2021-25. Last year, he started 14 games, including 12 at left tackle. Overall, he allowed 2.9 pressures per game, the second-highest rate among offensive linemen, only behind Tennessee's Dan Moore Jr., and nine sacks, tied for third-most. He also committed seven penalties. By the end of the season, the Jaguars had moved him to right guard and moved Van Lanen to left tackle.

But coach Liam Coen said last week, "I have a lot of confidence" in Little.

"I probably can't overstate how important it is because we really are fortunate to not have to play a backup in a situation when a tackle goes down," Coen said a day later. "I don't look at Walker as a backup tackle or a backup guard."

This -- plus calling up someone from the practice squad -- seems to be the clear solution for now, but if Little struggles, the Jaguars could pursue other options.

Move Cole Van Lanen to left tackle

Van Lanen impressed moving over to left tackle late last season, so much so that he got a three-year, $51 million extension. Should Coen and his staff deem it worth doing again, they already have proof of concept.

The issue, though, is that it would create a hole at right tackle, where Van Lanen has worked the past several months. Little stepped in for some snaps at right tackle in two games this season, but both times were at the end of blowouts. He has never played meaningful right tackle snaps in his NFL career, though the Jaguars clearly trusted him to do so, considering he was their swing tackle prior to Harrison's injury.

Trade for Fred Johnson or Andrew Wylie

Unfortunately for Jacksonville, it's not like capable left tackles are a dime a dozen. However, there are some options potentially available before the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

The Commanders and the Eagles are two potential sellers in the lowly NFC East. The Eagles have already traded away Cam Jurgens amid a nightmarish season for the entire organization. Last year, the Jaguars traded Fred Johnson to Philadelphia for a 2026 seventh-round pick. Might they be interested in a reunion?

Andrew Wylie is another name that could be of interest. He has not played meaningful snaps at left tackle, but he has played a ton at right tackle, right guard and left guard. If anything, he could be the Jaguars' swing tackle, the role Little had before Harrison's injury. Wylie has played sparingly this season, though it was at left tackle.

title: More Bad News For Rams: Star WR Puka Nacua Leaves Practice Early With Calf Injury
description:
As if things couldn’t get any worse for the Los Angeles Rams, they could now be without another star playmaker.
Star wide receiver Puka Nacua left Rams practice early on Thursday due to a calf injury, putting his status for Sunday's game against the Las Vegas Raiders into question.
Nacua was later listed as limited on the Rams' injury report.
The Rams' offense is already without wide receiver Davante Adams, who was placed on injured reserve with a ruptured hamstring.
With Adams sidelined for six to 10 weeks and Nacua now dealing with a calf injury, the injury list for Los Angeles continues to grow.
text:
As if things couldn’t get any worse for the Los Angeles Rams, they could now be without another star playmaker.

Star wide receiver Puka Nacua left Rams practice early on Thursday due to a calf injury, putting his status for Sunday's game against the Las Vegas Raiders into question. Nacua was later listed as limited on the Rams' injury report.

The Rams' offense is already without wide receiver Davante Adams, who was placed on injured reserve with a ruptured hamstring. With Adams sidelined for six to 10 weeks and Nacua now dealing with a calf injury, the injury list for Los Angeles continues to grow.

Nacua’s season has been plagued by injury trouble, as he already missed two games earlier this year with a hip issue.

When healthy, however, Nacua has been highly productive. He has hauled in 37 receptions for 417 yards and a touchdown across four games, highlighted by a showing against the Buffalo Bills where he caught a career-high 17 passes for 138 yards and a touchdown.

After entering the season as Super Bowl favorites due to their blockbuster offseason, it’s been a downward spiral for the Rams. Star edge rusher Myles Garrett hasn't played since Week 1 due to a knee injury that required surgery.

To top it off, the Rams sit at 2-4 and are already in a position where they must fight for a Wild Card spot in a crowded and competitive NFC.

If Nacua misses any time, the Rams' offense might have to lean heavily on backup wide receivers Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington and tight end Tyler Higbee as Matthew Stafford’s primary targets. Providing depth behind them are veteran Tutu Atwell and sixth-round pick CJ Daniels.

text:
Each practice day this season, the Kansas City Chiefs release an official injury report ahead of the next game. In Week 7, the Chiefs play the Seattle Seahawks on “Sunday Night Football.”

On Thursday, Kansas City placed left tackle Josh Simmons (Back) on the Reserve/Injured list after he didn’t practice on Wednesday. The Chiefs explained that Simmons plateaued in his rehabilitation and needed more time to return to 100%. For more information from the team’s Head Trainer Rick Burkholder, we covered his statement to local media here.

Here is the Chiefs’ first official injury report of the week, courtesy of the team’s official website:

Chiefs

Wide receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) did not participate in practice for the second consecutive day. He tweaked his hamstring during the first quarter of the Week 4 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. He did not have the “Knee” designation on the injury report until this week.

Right tackle Jaylon Moore (concussion) did not participate in practice again after entering the concussion protocol during the Week 6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers. Moore’s participation going forward is dependent on the contracted independent neurologist and completely out of the team and player’s hands.

Cornerback L’Jarius Sneed (knee) was a limited participant in practice again. His time on the field is regularly managed due to a lingering knee issue.

Tight end Travis Kelce (ankle) was a limited participant in practice again. Kelce briefly left in Week 6 against the Chargers and was seen multiple times having his ankle taped.

Linebacker Cooper McDonald (knee) was a limited participant in practice for the second straight day. McDonald was placed on the team’s Reserve/Injured list after suffering a knee injury in Week 1. Although he has been “designated to return,” McDonald must be officially added to the active roster by Saturday in order to play against Seattle. The Chiefs seemingly opened a roster spot for McDonald by waiving linebacker Cam Jones on Tuesday.

The following Chiefs players were full participants in practice:

Wide receiver Cyrus Allen (knee)

Safety Chamarri Conner (knee)

Right guard Trey Smith (hip)

Quarterback Patrick Mahomes (knee)

Seahawks

The team’s Senior Reporter John Boyle reported that running back Zach Charbonnet has been activated off the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list after full participation in Wednesday’s practice.

Charbonnet has not played since the Seahawks’ Divisional Round win over the San Francisco 49ers last season. The backfield partner of Kenneth Walker in 2025 racked up 874 yards and 12 touchdowns last season.

Veteran defensive end Demarcus Lawrence (non-injury related - rest) was a limited participant in practice on Thursday after sitting out on Wednesday.

Starting outside linebacker Uchenne Nwosu (hip) popped up on Thursday’s injury report as a limited participant after not appearing on the list on Wednesday.

Linebacker Connor O’Toole (hamstring), linebacker Chazz Surratt (calf) and linebacker Drake Thomas (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday’s ot Thursday’s practice.

Former Missouri quarterback, the backup to Sam Darnold, Drew Lock (right elbow) was a limited participant in practice on both days this week.

Wide receiver Rasheed Shaheed (hip), linebacker Tyrice Knight, and guards Anthony Bradford (knee) and Beau Stephens (knee) were full participants in Thursday’s practice after limited action on Wednesday.

Check back in on Friday afternoon for the final injury report.

text:
Arizona Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love is expected to miss Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos, according to CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz.

An ankle injury sidelined the first-round pick for Arizona's 18-16 win over the Los Angeles Rams in Week 6.

Bam Knight ran for 80 yards on 15 carries against L.A., and Tyler Allgeier chipped in with 38 yards on the ground.

The Broncos have been one of the NFL's worst teams against the run. They're 31st in yards allowed at 139.8 per game, and they're giving up 4.7 yards per carry.

The matchup would seemingly present a great opportunity for Love to get his rookie campaign on track after an inconsistent start. He has run for 245 yards and one touchdown while averaging 3.7 yards per carry in five appearances.

That's not the kind of return you want to see from a running back selected third overall.

Rather than taking advantage of Denver's porous defense, Love will have to wait another week to reestablish himself in Arizona's backfield.

Knight and Allgeier, meanwhile, have one more game to deliver the kind of performance that could force coach Mike LaFleur to rethink the hierarchy in the running game once Love is back healthy.

text:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — All-Pro Rams receiver Puka Nacua left practice early with a calf injury Thursday, creating yet another major injury concern for Los Angeles.

Nacua couldn't finish the Rams' second practice since they lost six-time Pro Bowl receiver Davante Adams for six to 10 weeks with a hamstring injury.

Nacua has 37 catches for 417 yards and a touchdown while playing in just four games this season for the Rams (2-4), who have lost three of four in a season that began with Super Bowl aspirations. Nacua missed two games last month with an injury centered in his groin and hip, but returned for their past three games.

Nacua is vital to the Rams in Adams' absence because they are relatively thin behind their two star wide receivers. The only other wideouts who have caught a pass for Los Angeles this season are second-year pro Konata Mumpfield, veteran Tutu Atwell and Jordan Whittington.

Nacua led the NFL with 129 receptions last season for 1,715 yards and 10 touchdowns. The 2023 fifth-round pick was one of the most productive receivers in NFL history during the first three seasons of his career, and he currently has 350 receptions for 4,608 yards and 20 touchdowns in just 48 regular-season games.

The Rams were labeled a super team and anointed as Super Bowl favorites at the start of the season, but injuries have played a major role in their inability to live up to those predictions.

AP NFL Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett made no tackles in his Rams debut before going on injured reserve for knee surgery, and he has yet to return to practice. Star cornerback Trent McDuffie missed last week's game with a groin injury that has kept him out of the Rams' first two practices this week, while key defensive linemen Kobie Turner and Poona Ford are also out with injuries.

The Rams lost 18-16 to rebuilding Arizona last Sunday. They travel to face the Las Vegas Raiders this Sunday.

The Philadelphia Eagles have been devastated by injuries this season, which has helped contribute to their extremely disappointing 2-4 start. They listed 24 players on their initial Thursday injury report. The Cowboys, conversely, are relatively healthy, but have also begun their season with a 2-4 record.

Here's the Eagles-Cowboys injury report, with analysis.

Thursday notes:

• DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, and Dallas Goedert all missed practice. That's bad news for the Eagles' already crappy passing attack.

• Nolan Smith had a scary-looking concussion Week 6 against the Panthers. It's no surprise that he did not practice. Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle), Jonathan Greenard (ankle), and A.J. Epenesa (back) were all limited with their injuries. The Eagles are obviously very banged-up on the edge.

• Moro Ojomo played through obvious pain against the Panthers. We now find out that it was an abdomen injury.

• Saquon Barkley practiced for the first time since injuring his hamstring Week 4 against the Rams, although he was limited. It is anticipated that he will play on Monday.

• Add a pectoral injury to Landon Dickerson's pre-existing knee injury.

• Tyler Steen was limited with his shoulder injury. He'll likely play.

• Drew Kendall was active Week 6 against the Panthers, but only as an emergency player. He was limited to start this week.

Notable players on IR, PUP, suspension, etc.

• QB Jalen Hurts (IR, season over): Hurts is out indefinitely with a superficial blood clot. Tanner McKee started against the Panthers, and will remain the starter against the Cowboys.

• LG Landon Dickerson (IR, eligible to return at any time): Dickerson had his worst game as a pro in the Eagles' Week 1 win over the Commanders, and was quickly thereafter placed on injured reserve. A lot of O-line juggling has ensued. The Eagles activated Dickerson's 21-day practice window last week.

• RB Tank Bigsby (IR, eligible to return after Week 8): Bigsby suffered an injury Week 4 against the Rams that required core muscle surgery. He will likely return this season, but could miss up to two months.

• RB Will Shipley (IR, eligible to return after Week 9): Shipley suffered a Lisfranc injury and will be out a while. Shipley is the Eagles' best RB in pass protection, but he only has 57 yards on 20 carries this season.

• TE Eli Stowers (IR, eligible to return at any time): The Eagles selected Stowers in the second round of the 2026 draft because of his athletic traits, but he did not have a good rookie training camp, and is not yet ready to play. He was listed as questionable on the Eagles' injury report with a hamstring injury heading into Week 1, but was moved to IR. The Eagles activated Stowers' 21-day practice window last week.

Thursday notes:

• Dee Winters is a starting linebacker. He was a free agent signing from the Niners this past offseason.

• KaVontae Turpin is perhaps the best return specialist in the NFL. He is not expected to play on Monday.

• The three most important Cowboys players who were limited on Thursday were WR George Pickens, LT Tyler Guyton, and CB Cobie Durant. We'll monitor their progress leading up to gameday.

Notable players on IR, PUP, suspension, etc.

• S Jalen Thompson (IR): The Cowboys signed Thompson to a three-year deal worth up to $33 million. He was probably their biggest free agent signing this offseason, and their only starter on IR. Thompson had a productive three-year stretch from 2021 to 2023, when he had 8 INTs and averaged over 100 tackles per season. However, in the last two seasons, Thompson has 0 INTs and 1 FF. He is on IR with a hamstring injury.

• S P.J. Locke (IR): Locke is a role player in the Cowboys' secondary. He suffered a foot injury Week 2 and landed on IR.

• LB Marist Liufau (IR): Liufau played in all 17 games each of his first two seasons in the NFL in 2024 and 2025. He has 14 career starts. In two seasons he has 80 tackles, 2.5 sacks, 3 pass breakups and 2 forced fumbles. He broke his forearm in a preseaosn game and has not yet played this season. He would be a backup and special teams guy, if healthy.

• DL Jonathan Bullard (IR): Rotational DL. 3 tackles and a half sack in 3 games this season.

• RB Malik Davis (IR): Davis suffered a serious hip injury before the start of the season, and his season is over. In 2025, he had 52 carries for 250 yards and 2 TDs.

• CB Devin Moore (IR): Fourth-round rookie, groin injury, hasn't yet played.

Bears tight end Cole Kmet appears to have suffered a very serious injury during Thursday night’s win over the Patriots.

Coach Ben Johnson said after the game that nothing will be definitively diagnosed until Friday, but the early indications were that it’s a bad injury.

“We’ll know more about it tomorrow, but I don’t think it looked very good,” Johnson said.

Bears quarterback Caleb Williams said it hurt to see a player who means so much to him carted off the field.

“It was tough. I don’t know exactly what it is, but getting carted off is never good. You’re at least going to miss some time. I don’t have the words to describe what Cole is to me, to this team, to this organization. He’s the longest-tenured Bear, I believe,” Williams said. “He’s been through it and it’s challenging. It’s tough. I’ll be right there with him through every step of whatever the injury is. Cole’s been there for me every step of the way, through the first year, through the second year, and now through this year. I could only do the same for him.”

text:
The San Francisco 49ers are thriving at 6-0 entering Sunday's showdown against the Atlanta Falcons.

They're coming off a 23-17 victory over the Washington Commanders on Monday night and are now one of three remaining unbeaten teams in the NFL.

However, San Francisco is still navigating the injury bug. Veteran wide receiver Mike Evans' status for Week 7 is in doubt after he left Monday's game with an Achilles issue he was already dealing with before kickoff.

49ers GM Announces Update on Evans

Although the injury doesn't appear serious, 49ers general manager John Lynch discussed Evans' status during his weekly appearance on KNBR.

Lynch said Evans' status remains undetermined and noted that he "wouldn't say it's not likely" that the wide receiver suits up Sunday.

"I wouldn't say not likely, I think it's still TBD," Lynch said. "We've got a couple more days, we're going to take every bit of those. He's done a really good job treating this thing and we know of Mike's toughness… He's that type of player that you wait and let it play itself out."

The 49ers have a bye next week, so Evans could get two weeks of rest if the team chooses to sit him. Lynch was asked about that possibility Thursday, as fans have urged San Francisco to rest the veteran wide receiver while the team remains 6-0.

"I absolutely love our fans… There's gonna be noise, our job is not to focus on the noise but to focus on what we believe is right for our football team and that's what we continue to do," Lynch added.

Evans' Practice Status

Now in his 13th NFL season, Evans has become such a veteran that he doesn't necessarily need extensive practice time to suit up for a game.

He showed that last week when he barely practiced while managing his ongoing rib injury and Achilles soreness. However, he played Monday night and recorded three receptions for 94 yards before exiting in the second quarter.

Evans didn't practice Wednesday, and it's unlikely he'll do much Thursday either.

text:
CHICAGO -- Bears tight end Cole Kmet exited Chicago's 30-24 win over the New England Patriots on Thursday night on a cart because of an injury to his right knee.

With 5:46 to play in the fourth quarter, Kmet caught an 8-yard pass from Caleb Williams and took a hard hit while running up the Bears' sideline. The tight end collided with Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez and linebacker Robert Spillane, and immediately grabbed for his knee while on the ground.

Kmet got to his feet with the help of trainers but could not put weight on his right leg. He gave the crowd at Soldier Field a thumbs-up as he was carted back to the locker room, where he was quickly ruled out for the remainder of the game.

Coach Ben Johnson said the Bears will find out more about the severity of Kmet's injury on Friday.

"I don't think it looked very good," Johnson said.

Williams had a similar response after watching Kmet leave the game with what appeared to be a serious injury.

"It was tough," Williams said. "I don't know exactly what it is and all of that, but obviously being carted off is never good. You're at least going to miss some time. I don't have the words to describe what Cole is to me, what Cole is to this team, this organization. He's the longest-tenured Bear, I believe. And so he's been through it, and it's challenging, it's tough and I'll be with him. I'll be right there with him through every step of whatever the injury is. And Cole's been there for me every step of the way through the first year, the second year and now through this year. I could only do the same for him."

Kmet finished with three catches for 28 yards. Entering Week 7, he had logged the eighth-highest snap count on offense, and he has missed only one game over his seven-year career due to injury.

text:
The Seahawks announced a couple of roster transactions ahead of their Week 7 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs. The happy and expected news was Zach Charbonnet being activated from the PUP list. The bad news is Elijah Arroyo has been placed on injured reserve. ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on Thursday that Arroyo will have to undergo shoulder surgery and will miss the rest of the 2026 NFL season.

Arroyo injured his shoulder last week against the Denver Broncos while attempting to recover Rashid Shaheed’s fumble. Coming out of the Broncos game, it did not sound positive. In fact, an injured reserve stint was expected for Arroyo. That his season is already over is surely a big blow for the second-year tight end out of Miami.

Arroyo had an electric 2026 training camp, which brought a lot of optimism that Arroyo could have a big sophomore jump this season. Unfortunately this strong training camp did not continue into the regular season. Arroyo has seldom seen any targets this season and will finish his 2026 season with only one catch for 17 yards and 0 touchdowns.

Entering the draft, Arroyo was heralded for his pass catching ability. However, with questions around his blocking ability and injury history (including an ACL tear), Arroyo managed to slip to Seattle at 50th overall. Unfortunately, the injury concerns have continued for Arroyo into the NFL. Arroyo missed the back-end of the 2025 regular season after injuring his knee in Week 14.

As for the Seahawks, their tight end room is left with AJ Barner, Eric Saubert, and Nick Kallerup on the 53-man roster, with Josiah Deguara recently joining the practice squad. Saubert and Kallerup are known for their blocking rather than receiving abilities. Because of this, Seattle could potentially add a bigger pass catcher to the active roster.

text:
RENTON, Wash. -- The Seattle Seahawks activated running back Zach Charbonnet off the physically unable to perform list Thursday, an expected move amid his comeback from a torn ACL.

It's not certain that Charbonnet, who is only eight months removed from surgery, will make his season debut Sunday night when the Seahawks host the Kansas City Chiefs at Lumen Field. Coach Mike Macdonald said earlier this week that it's a "possibility" that he plays "in some capacity."

The Seahawks listed Charbonnet as a full participant in practice Wednesday and Thursday.

"Just taking it a day at a time," Charbonnet said Thursday in his first comments to reporters since he was injured in January. "But whenever I'm out there, it's going to be special and I'm just going to be happy to get back out there."

The Seahawks on Thursday also placed second-year tight end Elijah Arroyo on injured reserve. A source told ESPN's Adam Schefter that Arroyo, a 2025 second-round pick who caught one pass for 17 yards in six games this season, is having season-ending surgery to repair a shoulder injury he suffered last week in a loss to the Denver Broncos.

Charbonnet had been listed as limited on the first eight injury reports released by the team since it designated him to return to practice Oct. 1. Thursday marked the 21-day deadline to move Charbonnet to the 53-man roster.

In a co-starting role last season alongside Kenneth Walker III, Charbonnet rushed for 730 yards and a team-high 12 touchdowns. He tore his left ACL in Seattle's divisional round win over the San Francisco 49ers on Jan. 17 and had surgery Feb. 12.

Charbonnet said this was "around" the time that he was aiming to return.

"I'm feeling pretty good," Charbonnet said. "Just going a day at a time. Seeing how it adapts with picking up practice and stuff like that."

With Charbonnet beginning the season on PUP and rookie first-round pick Jadarian Price missing the last three games with a chest injury, Seattle is averaging 107.2 rushing yards per game and 3.9 yards per carry, both of which rank 18th. Their backfield trio of Price, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani have combined to lose four fumbles.

Price, who was placed on IR in Week 4, has to miss at least one more game.

text:
The Bears will be without mainstay linebacker T.J. Edwards on Thursday against the Patriots. It’s Edwards’ second consecutive game sidelined by a hamstring injury.

The Bears also will miss backup linebacker Jack Sanborn (concussion) and likely will start Devin Bush and D’Marco Jackson.

They won’t have No. 2 running back Kyle Monangai for the third game in a row, leaving a share of the carries for Roschon Johnson. Monangai has been on the injury report with thumb and toe injuries, though coach Ben Johnson has said the thumb isn’t a significant concern.

Those issues have kept him out since rushing for 146 yards and two touchdowns on 30 carries against the Jets on Oct. 4.

The good news for the Bears is that right guard Jonah Jackson will play through a hip injury that took him out of the Falcons game last week.

text:
LOS ANGELES -- Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua left Thursday's practice with a calf injury, a team spokesperson said.

Nacua was listed on the injury report as a limited participant in Thursday's practice.

The Rams were already without wide receiver Davante Adams, who injured his hamstring in their Week 6 loss to the Arizona Cardinals. Adams will miss six to 10 weeks with the injury, coach Sean McVay said Monday.

Nacua missed the Rams' Week 2 and 3 games with a psoas injury. In four games this season, Nacua has 37 catches for 417 yards and a touchdown.

Nacua is the latest in a long list of injury updates this week. Along with Adams, the Rams are without nose tackle Poona Ford, who will miss the rest of the season with a ruptured triceps, and defensive tackle Kobie Turner, who will miss "a handful of weeks" with a groin injury. The Rams also lost kicker Blake Grupe to a torn ACL in Week 6.

authors: Cameron DaSilva, Rams Wire, Cameron DaSilva, Rams Wire
description:
After already losing several starters to injured reserve this week, the Los Angeles Rams took another hit on offense Thursday.
According to reporters, Puka Nacua left practice early after suffering a calf injury.
Nacua dealt with a hip/groin injury earlier this season, missing two games in Weeks 2 and 3.
Davante Adams is already on IR with a ruptured hamstring, so Los Angeles can't afford to lose Nacua, too.
After practice on Friday, the Rams will release their final injury report with game statuses for Nacua and any other players who are banged up.
text:
After already losing several starters to injured reserve this week, the Los Angeles Rams took another hit on offense Thursday. According to reporters, Puka Nacua left practice early after suffering a calf injury. He was officially a limited participant in practice, though the severity of the injury is not yet known.

Sean McVay will address the media on Friday, at which point he will provide an update on the Rams' star receiver.

Nacua dealt with a hip/groin injury earlier this season, missing two games in Weeks 2 and 3. He returned in Week 4 and picked up right where he left off with back-to-back 100-yard games against the Eagles and Bills.

The Rams are set to take on the Raiders this Sunday in a pivotal Week 7 game. Davante Adams is already on IR with a ruptured hamstring, so Los Angeles can't afford to lose Nacua, too.

After practice on Friday, the Rams will release their final injury report with game statuses for Nacua and any other players who are banged up.

Bengals vs. Ravens Injury Report
text:
The Cincinnati Bengals are looking good on the injury front as they prepare for a big AFC North clash with the Baltimore Ravens. On the other side, Baltimore may have a chance to get their franchise quarterback back on the field, according to Thursday's reporting.

For the Bengals, safety Kyle Dugger (quad) was upgraded to a full participant on Thursday. It is unknown whether he will play on Sunday, but he appears to be trending toward a return after being out since Week 3.

Defensive tackles Jonathan Allen and B.J. Hill both got a veteran's rest day.

For Baltimore, quarterback Lamar Jackson (ankle) was listed as a limited participant Thursday. On Wednesday, he was listed as limited as well, but it sounds like he got a decent amount more work done in Thursday's practice.

Media members reported Jackson was active in practice and wasn't seen favoring the ankle that has kept him out of the lineup since October 4th. Media wasn't present for the entire practice, so that reporting is essentially just from warmups.

Baltimore's new center Cam Jergens (concussion) was a full participant for the second day in a row. If he clears the NFL's concussion protocol, he should make his Ravens debut on Sunday.

Safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) was downgraded to a nonparticipant after being limited on Wednesday, so his availability for Sunday is in question.

Linebacker Tavius Robinson (pectoral) was also out.

text:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. (KCTV) - Kansas City Chiefs left tackle Josh Simmons is being placed on injured reserve due to a back injury that has sidelined him for more than two months.

On Thursday, Chiefs Vice President of Sports Medicine and Performance Rick Burkholder shared details of Simmons’ injury timeline and next steps with the media.

Burkholder said Simmons -- who has dealt with a bulging disc in his lower back since training camp -- will go on injured reserve after practicing in a limited capacity last week.

Burkholder said the Chiefs, Simmons and his representation decided the 2025 first-round pick should go on injured reserve because they determined he had stalled in his rehab process.

“We feel that he’s plateaued in the rehab process, as he’s trying to get to the final steps of recovery with return to competition,” Burkholder said. “And he’s just not there yet.”

Burkholder said Simmons came to him on Aug. 17 following a training camp practice in which he felt trouble in his calf area on the same leg he tore his patellar tendon in college. An MRI conducted in St. Joseph, Missouri, determined Simmons had a bulging, herniated disc in his lumbar spine. Burkholder said the disc problem was higher up than the team typically sees in offensive linemen, “which complicated the case.”

A second opinion with a spine specialist in California determined rehab, rather than surgery, was recommended.

“A few weeks later,” Burkholder said, “the repeat MRI a few weeks later showed that the disc had improved, so no surgery was recommended and rehab would continue.”

Burkholder said Simmons’ rehab was diligent, but the lack of progress has now resulted in the team making a move.

“Josh worked his tail off,” Burkholder said. “He worked diligently with my staff every day and has improved to the point where he returned to practice in a limited capacity last week.”

Simmons was listed as a non-participant in Wednesday’s practice as the Chiefs prepare for a ‘Sunday Night Football’ matchup with the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. The Chiefs listed Simmons’ absence as due to “back/personal,” which Burkholder said was to give Simmons “some time to talk with his family and his representatives to investigate next steps as he goes through this process.”

That process led to the decision to place Simmons on injured reserve, though Simmons still does not need surgery.

“He’ll continue with the rehab process with the goal of returning to play at a high level that he achieved in the past,” Burkholder said. “I just give (Simmons) a ton of credit for navigating through this injury to the point where surgery is not recommended and that he needs more time to return to full function.”

Now, Simmons will not be eligible to return for at least four games, meaning the Ohio State product who has missed 14 of a possible 22 games during his career will not be allowed to play until at least a Week 11 matchup with the Arizona Cardinals.

Without Simmons, undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson has started at left tackle in each of Kansas City’s first five games.
